test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 06 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 18 years more than 4 times the present age of the son. After 5 years, 4 times the father's age will be 8 years less than 14 times the son's age. The difference (in years) between the present ages of the father and the son is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From the first condition: **Father + Son** = 4 × **Son** + 18 ⇒ **Father** = 3 × **Son** + 18.

Substitute this into the second condition: 4(3 × **Son** + 18 + 5) = 14(**Son** + 5) − 8.

⇒ 12 × **Son** + 92 = 14 × **Son** + 62 ⇒ 2 × **Son** = 30 ⇒ **Son** = 15 years.

**Father** = 3(15) + 18 = 63 years.

Difference = 63 − 15 = 48 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the **present age** of the **father** be F and the **son** be S.

Equation 1: F + S = 4S + 18

Equation 2: 4(F + 5) = 14(S + 5) − 8

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ca6803d0ac4cc8884882c7e83e19472c887bb27637f207273647ac5b61683db.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ F − 3S = 18 ··· (i)

⇒ 4F + 20 = 14S + 70 − 8

⇒ 4F − 14S = 42

⇒ 2F − 7S = 21 ··· (ii)

Multiply (i) by 2:

⇒ 2F − 6S = 36 ··· (iii)

Subtract (ii) from (iii):

⇒ (2F − 6S) − (2F − 7S) = 36 − 21

⇒ S = 15 years

Substitute S = 15 in (i):

⇒ F − 3(15) = 18

⇒ F = 18 + 45 = 63 years

⇒ Difference = F − S = 63 − 15 = 48 years

**∴ The correct answer is 48 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Age Difference Constant

The numerical difference between the ages of two persons always remains the same, regardless of how many years pass.

Linear Equation Formation

For age problems, always define present ages as variables (X, Y) and adjust for 'n' years ago (X−n) or 'n' years later (X+n).

Ratio of Ages

If the ratio of ages is given as a:b, we can assume ages to be ax and bx to simplify the equations.</p
